comparison_explanation: Candidate A (id 3) is the better generalizing model. It achieves a substantially higher adjusted R-squared (0.598 vs 0.467) and a lower validation RMSE (0.1557 vs 0.1786), while all five predictors are statistically significant and its maximum VIF of 5.29 remains below the conventional 10.0 threshold. Candidate B (id 5) has even lower multicollinearity (max VIF 1.40) and all predictors significant, but its predictive performance is materially weaker. Therefore Candidate A is ranked first despite its somewhat higher but still acceptable collinearity.
risks: The model is observational and cannot support causal claims about crime.
PctIlleg may act as a broad proxy for concentrated socioeconomic disadvantage and could raise interpretation/endogeneity concerns.
Max VIF is moderate (5.29); acceptable below 10, but higher than the alternative candidate.
Validation RMSE of about 0.156 on a 0-1 normalized target still leaves meaningful unexplained variance.
Variables come from different years/sources (1990 Census, LEMAS, FBI UCR), which may introduce measurement timing mismatch.
